title: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement
abstract: arXiv:2611.33050v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once. Blind preference votes, which rank these models, are read as judgments of their text, and if delivery matters, faster answers are expected to gain. Research on the labor illusion and on how text appears on screen suggests instead that an answer which unfolds as it is written is credited over the same answer shown at once. We test these accounts with three sources of variation in natural use. First, compar:IA, a French government chatbot arena, answered repeated prompts, by a random draw, either with a fresh answer streamed as it was written or with a stored earlier answer from the same model, shown at once. translated_title: 值得等待吗？响应时间与流式呈现如何塑造对生成式AI答案的评价及聊天机器人的使用
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的生成式AI聊天机器人如今以截然不同的速度给出回答：推理模型在回复前会进行深思熟虑，而响应缓存则能立即返回存储的答案。对这些模型进行排名的盲选偏好投票通常被解读为对其文本质量的判断，但如果呈现方式也很重要，那么更快的答案理应更受青睐。然而，关于“劳动错觉”的研究以及关于文本在屏幕上如何呈现的研究表明，边写边展开显示的答案反而比一次性完整显示的相同答案更受好评。我们利用自然使用中的变异来源检验了这些理论。首先，compar:IA（一个法国政府的聊天机器人竞技场）对重复的提示词，通过随机抽签，要么以正在撰写时逐字流式输出的全新答案作答，要么一次性显示来自同一模型的先前存储的答案。在相同的提示词下，回放式（一次性显示的存储）答案在决定性盲选投票中获胜的概率降低了25.8个百分点。
tldr: 本文通过法国政府聊天机器人竞技场的自然实验发现，边写边流式输出的答案比同一模型一次性显示的相同存储答案在盲选投票中获胜概率高出25.8个百分点，证明答案的呈现方式（而不仅是内容）显著影响用户对生成式AI的评价。
en_tdlr: Through a natural experiment on the French government chatbot arena compar:IA, this paper shows that streaming an answer as it is written outperforms displaying the same stored answer at once—replays lose 25.8 percentage points in decisive blind votes—demonstrating that response delivery, not just content, shapes judgments of generative AI answers.
